issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with three parameters (String, int, int), but the template's StockIngredient class only provides a four-parameter constructor (String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This mismatch will confuse students about which constructor to use and may cause compilation or implementation issues when they follow the UML/solution expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template match the UML and solution by providing a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). Either replace the existing four-argument constructor with a three-argument one or add a three-argument overload that delegates to the existing constructor (e.g., new StockIngredient(name, price, quantity, false)). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to reflect the four-argument constructor if that was intentional.
